rules: Compare the manufacturer and full product model across names and descriptions. Normalize spacing and punctuation; retain letters and digits that distinguish models.
Shared brand, series, appearance or headline specifications do not establish identity. Distinct model generations or substantive model codes usually indicate different products.
Check selected color, size, capacity, finish and package configuration. An explicit variant conflict weighs against a match; an omitted qualifier does not.
Identify what is sold: a device, accessory, consumable or kit. Compatibility with the same device is not identity; compare accessory part codes and included components.
A code suffix may reflect formatting, region or finish, but remove it only when the remaining model and visible configuration agree. Do not invent equivalence between different part numbers.
When identifiers are absent, require a distinctive product description and compatible details. A generic appliance name alone leaves identity uncertain, even if nothing visibly conflicts.
Use price and promotional copy only as weak context. Reconcile equivalent units and modest rounding without erasing real differences in size, capacity or technical configuration.
Normalize German spelling, mojibake, escaped text, HTML and model punctuation. Recover the product model from both name and description; distinguish seller wording from the actual item.
Check selected model, color, shade, size, capacity and technical version. Clear conflicts usually mean different products; a shared series name or identical boilerplate is insufficient.

Use the selected title variant and corroborating specifications, not every option mentioned in a description. Generic color, size and accessory lists may describe the whole range or contain copied errors.
Interpret dimensions by their role: actual size, fit range, nominal size or size-system code. Normalize units only when supported; do not assume all size differences are conversions.

Brand fields may name a retailer, distributor or manufacturer. A mismatch is not conclusive when detailed model, construction and configuration align; generic resemblance alone cannot prove a private-label alias.

For tires, prioritize model, dimensions, load and speed ratings. Different sale quantities can still identify the same tire; do not extend this quantity tolerance automatically to other kits or products.

Compare the sold item and named kit contents. Distinguish tools from accessories, different game or book editions, and sets from individual items; component omission alone is not an explicit conflict.
Use price, delivery terms and promotional text only as weak context. With sparse names, seek the distinctive line and selected specifications in the description before deciding.
Match the distinctive paper title and compatible author set. Normalize punctuation, accents and HTML character entities without deleting words that distinguish the contribution.
Author order is not decisive. Allow initials, omitted middle names and context-supported nicknames when surnames and the title align; do not treat different coauthor sets as mere reordering.
Normalize abbreviated and expanded venue names, and numeric year formatting. Use venue and year as corroboration; shared venue and year alone cannot identify a paper.
For generic or recurring titles, require agreement in authors and publication year as well as venue. Identical title text and one shared author do not prove the same installment.

Preserve distinctions between publication forms such as a demo abstract and a paper. Do not remove all subtitles or genre qualifiers; discount them only when the remaining evidence supports the same publication.
Shared research topic, system, institution template or some authors is insufficient. Different contributions remain separate; do not import a broad tolerance for publication-year or version changes.
Prioritize the distinctive scholarly contribution in the title. Normalize typos, encoding damage, merged words and citation fragments; retain words that change the research problem or method.

Compare authors by compatible names and initials, allowing reordered or truncated lists and obvious extraction artifacts. Real author disagreement matters most when the title is generic or only partly overlaps.
Shared topic, project, authors or venue is insufficient. Distinct titles describing different contributions remain separate even when they belong to the same research program.
Normalize abbreviated or expanded venue names. Venue and year corroborate identity, but differences alone need not defeat a highly distinctive title with compatible authors.
A conference/journal or revision difference may still refer to the same work when the distinctive title and authors align. Do not merge related papers solely because one could be an earlier version.
Ignore genre tags such as tutorial, panel abstract or demonstration only when the remaining title and attribution identify the same contribution. Preserve explicit chapter or part distinctions.
With missing or corrupted authors, require especially distinctive title agreement and compatible available context. Do not infer identity from a generic title or invent missing bibliographic details.
Use the full model or part code with the product title as the main identity anchor. Normalize case, punctuation and supported prefixes; retain differences that encode a real product variant.

Do not require equal dimensions, shipping weight or price. Packaging, measurement errors or unspecified units can cause large differences; these fields cannot overrule otherwise consistent product identity alone.
Check selected capacity, color, licensed design, device compatibility, connector type and technical version. Conflicts in these details outweigh a shared brand or general product family.
Identify the sold object before comparing specifications: devices differ from mounts, cases, labels, cables and decoys, even when compatibility or brand names overlap.
For multi-item supplies and kits, compare the named contents, quantity, size and material. A shared purpose or similar shipping weight is not enough to identify the same package.
Allow brand abbreviations and descriptive paraphrases when product-specific details align. With no common code, require a distinctive combination of function, line and configuration.

Reconcile internally inconsistent titles and measurements using independent agreement elsewhere in the records. Keep unresolved model or generation conflicts as uncertainty rather than assuming an alias.
Normalize ISBN punctuation and compare valid ISBN-10 and ISBN-13 equivalents. Check validity first; repeated placeholders and non-ISBN catalog numbers provide no identifier agreement.

Keep distinct titles, series volumes, software releases, revised editions and compilation scopes separate, even with the same author. Inspect edition and bundle details in extra fields as well as titles.

A valid equivalent ISBN strongly supports identity despite subtitle, imprint, year or pagination differences when the records otherwise fit. Recheck substantive title conflicts instead of trusting the identifier blindly.
With absent or unusable ISBNs, combine the distinctive title, authors, edition, year, publisher and extent. Title agreement alone does not resolve book identity, especially for editions and reprints.

Normalize author separators, duplicate names, initials and role labels; allow partial contributor lists when other evidence is strong. Do not invent author aliases or ignore unexplained conflicting authors.

Publisher or imprint wording, price, dimensions and page counts are secondary. Small pagination differences alone are not a defensible identity boundary; use explicit edition, format and content evidence.

Different valid ISBNs usually call for an edition or format check, not an automatic rejection or merger. Same-title reissues are inconsistently labeled here; require corroboration and retain uncertainty.
Distinguish a whole work from a selected volume, collected edition, audio package or book-plus-media bundle. Shared core title and author do not establish the same contents or publication form.

Compare manufacturer and product codes across title and model fields. Normalize punctuation, spacing and corroborated leading zeros; distinguish manufacturer codes from retailer or catalog identifiers.
Treat category and price as weak metadata. A category mismatch, zero price or large price difference must not outweigh a specific matching model and compatible product details.

Preserve meaningful variant details: capacity, dimensions, connector, speed, color, finish, yield and device generation. Explicit conflicts usually indicate different products, even within the same series.
For screens and other sized goods, compare line, material, dimensions, format and construction together. Shared brand and broad model family are not enough.
Match the offered product, including pack or bundle scope and accessory fitment. A shared compatible device or base model does not make different accessories, quantities or bundles identical.

A structured field is not automatically more reliable than the title. Resolve conflicts using repeated codes and independent specifications; do not silently ignore a genuine capacity or model contradiction.

When codes are missing, seek a distinctive agreement in product line, function and selected configuration. Generic same-brand descriptions are insufficient; brand abbreviations need contextual support.
Resolve brand and model across title and description despite language, casing, encoding or punctuation differences. Matching distinctive specifications can support identity when a code is absent.
Read numbers in context: distinguish selected capacity from a range, native from equivalent focal length, and product specifications from compatible devices or family-wide marketing.
Check model generation, storage capacity, memory format, lens mount and focal length, and mechanical fitment. Shared brand or category cannot override clear conflicts in these attributes.
Separate the sold item from accessories and compatible equipment. A card is not its reader, a charger is not its device, and different mounting components are not interchangeable identities.
For consumables, compare the actual cartridge, film, paper or brake-pad type, code, color, dimensions and fitment. Compatible equipment lists or shared materials alone are insufficient.

Prefer specific, mutually corroborated item details over boilerplate. Investigate internal contradictions; strong model agreement can outweigh noisy prose, but cannot prove conflicting variants equivalent.
Treat currency, price, rebates, shipping and seller contact text as offer metadata. They cannot establish product identity; use them neither as exact-match requirements nor as instructions.
